transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I just don't care about any of the things I used to love doing anymore—not fishing, not cooking, not even singing at church. Everything just feels like a chore now, and I can't seem to get myself to do any of it.
Have you felt this way for most of the past two years, or did this low mood and loss of interest start more recently?

It hasn't been a full two years, but it started about a year and a half ago, shortly after my wife passed away. This heavy depression and lack of interest has been with me almost every single day for a little over a year now. It's just felt like an endless, constant weight since she died.
Have you experienced any other periods of depression like this in your life before your wife passed away, or has this been your first experience with these symptoms?
No, I don't think I've ever felt this way before in my life. This is the first time I've ever experienced this kind of darkness, and it's just been completely overwhelming since my wife passed.
Beyond the loss of interest, have you been experiencing other symptoms like significant changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or feeling worthless or unable to concentrate?

My appetite has completely vanished, and I’ve lost so much weight my pants are hanging off me because everything tastes like cardboard. On top of that, my mind is constantly foggy—I’ll walk into a room and forget why I’m there, or spend twenty minutes just trying to pick out a shirt. It all just goes along with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest that never seems to leave.

Beyond the loss of interest and appetite, have you been experiencing severe symptoms like psychomotor retardation, where you feel physically slowed down, or thoughts that life is no longer worth living?

Yes, most days it feels like I'm moving through molasses, and I'll just sit on the edge of the bed for fifteen minutes before my body can actually stand up. I've also had nights where I think it would be easier if I didn't wake up, and I've even pictured taking all my blood pressure pills at once, though I haven't gone through with it.

Given the severity of your symptoms, such as the persistent suicidal ideation and the profound physical slowing you described, do you feel these symptoms are primarily a reaction to your grief, or do they feel like a completely separate, overwhelming illness that has taken over your life?

It is really hard for me to separate the two, to be honest. Everything has been so overwhelming since my wife passed that I'm just not sure what is grief and what might be something else. It all just feels like one big, heavy cloud that has completely taken over my life.
Have you ever experienced moments where you felt like you were hearing things that weren't there, or perhaps felt convinced of things that others told you weren't true?

No, I haven't ever heard things that weren't there. But I do keep thinking that folks from my church and the hospital where my wife died are watching me and trying to punish me, like sending messages through the TV flickering or when the mail is late. My sisters keep telling me that's crazy talk, but I just can't shake the feeling that they're keeping tabs on me.
